title: Draft: HTTP3: enable dissection of headers via nghttp3
description:
HTTP3: enable dissection of headers via nghttp3

This PR adds basic dissection of HTTP3 headers. It uses nghttp3 for QPACK
inflation. Each HTTP3 connection has a pair of `nghttp3_qpack_decoder`
instances, which inflate the HEADERS frames sent by the client and the server.

Each decoder receives contents of the corresponding QPACK encoder stream.

When dissecting HEADERS frames, the dissector uses the appropriate decoder
to inflate the compressed header fields.

The dissector have been developed on OSX machine, and I have not tested it
on Linux or Windows.

To keep the pull request small and focused, many desired features are left
out of this pull request, and will be addressed in separate PRs later.
These include:

1. Occasionally the HEADERS frames are head-of-line blocked by the QPACK
   encoder stream. This happens when decoding of the headers depends on
   a QPACK instruction which the dissector have not seen yet.

2. Contents of the QPACK streams (both the encoder and decoder) are not
   properly dissected - the dissector doesn't show the invidual QPACK
   instructions.

3. This PR does not add dissection of other frame types (e.g SETTINGS).

4. Unlike the more mature HTTP2 dissector, this PR does not provide
   deduplication of repeating HTTP headers. Because of that, the memory
   usage is fairly high.

This PR includes design notes in `doc/http3.md`

Note: this PR is a re-submit of https://code.wireshark.org/review/#/c/38227/

The following comments are addressed:

- https://code.wireshark.org/review/#/c/38227/1/CMakeLists.txt@587
- https://code.wireshark.org/review/#/c/38227/1/CMakeLists.txt@608
- https://code.wireshark.org/review/#/c/38227/1/CMakeLists.txt@1654
- https://code.wireshark.org/review/#/c/38227/1/CMakeOptions.txt@97
- https://code.wireshark.org/review/#/c/38227/1/cmake/modules/FindNGHTTP3.cmake@25
- https://code.wireshark.org/review/#/c/38227/1/doc/http3.md@173
- https://code.wireshark.org/review/#/c/38227/1/epan/dissectors/packet-http3.c@157
- https://code.wireshark.org/review/#/c/38227/1/epan/dissectors/packet-http3.c@593
- https://code.wireshark.org/review/#/c/38227/1/tools/macos-setup-brew.sh@23


The best way to pull the `nghttp3` dependency remains an open question. Discussion at https://code.wireshark.org/review/#/c/38227/ mentioned two alternatives:
   a. Pull the commit tag instead of the release in `macos-setup.sh`
   b. Include a snapshot of nghttp3 in the Wireshark tree. 

I would like to get more feedback on which way is preferred.

P.S. There is an overlap between the HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 dissectors. Once the HTTP/3 dissector becomes more mature, it may be worthwhile to extract the shared dissection functionality from the HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 dissectors. At the moment, the HTTP/3 implementation is still nascent, hence I chose to keep the two implementations separate.

I have yet to review the new version, but to comment on the nghttp3 dep question, I'd be fine with a commit in setup-brew.sh instead of a git submodule. That'll be used for the official macos builds.

According to @alagoutte it seems like nghttp3 is not widely available yet. I'm fine providing a pre compiled library for Windows also but if it lets Linux users with the task to compile and install the library by themselves, maybe we should vendor it (at least at the begining). Note that I have not checked its size: if its huge then I'm less inclined to package it.

For me it meant checking a snapshot of the library to avoid using submodules.
When I download the nghttp3 source code and check the size of the lib folder, I get 662.3 Kbytes so I'm not sue how you got 8.5M (did you exclud the .git folder)?

I took a closer look, and a lot of space was used by the output of `autoconf`, such `autom4te.cache`, as well as the `.git` folder. I did a fresh `git clone` and checked the size. After excluding the `.git` folder, I get 1.1 MB for the entire `nghttp3` folder, breaking down into:

```
  ➜  ~/git/nghttp3_fresh ☠  du -I .git -h .
 12K	./cmake
184K	./tests
 56K	./examples
 64K	./lib/includes/nghttp3
 72K	./lib/includes
804K	./lib
 24K	./m4
1.1M	.
```

Previously the nghttp2 soures were checked into the tree, but to avoid "bundling" (something that Fedora and some other Linux distros dislike) it was dropped from the tree. I would try to avoid bundling the nghttp3 code with the Wireshark sources since it is likely going to cause noisy static code analyzer warnings that we should not care too much about.

Making it an optional dependency and let the Linux users without nghttp3 suffer sounds reasonable to me :) If needed, Linux distributions can built it themselves. It should be relatively straightforward for Flatpak builds for example. I am an Arch user and have a nghttp3 build somewhere and can surely use that for my development builds.
Fine by me, I'm gonna prepare a Windows library latter this week.

It seems that the consensus is to extend the `setup_macos.sh` script, so that it will use the stable hash of the library. 

I will do that soon.

I have tested this on Arch Linux using the latest nghttp3 git master, GCC 10.2.0 and Clang 10.0.1 with ASAN enabled. No memory leaks or other memory safety issues were detected in my test sample. Build config:
```
cd /path/to/nghttp3
prefix=/tmp/nghttp3-gcc; cmake -GNinja -S . -B "$prefix" -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$prefix/prefix" \
    -DENABLE_LIB_ONLY=1 -DENABLE_ASAN=1 && ninja -C "$prefix" install
prefix=/tmp/nghttp3-clang; cmake -GNinja -S . -B "$prefix" -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="$prefix/prefix" \
    -DENABLE_LIB_ONLY=1 -DENABLE_ASAN=1 -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ && \
    ninja -C "$prefix" install

# replace /tmp/ws-review with the path to this MR branch
mkdir /tmp/wsbuild-gcc && cd /tmp/wsbuild-gcc
PKG_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/nghttp3-gcc/prefix/lib/pkgconfig cmake -GNinja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
    -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=1 -DDISABLE_WERROR=1 -DENABLE_ASAN=1 -DENABLE_UBSAN=1 \
    /tmp/ws-review && time ninja

mkdir /tmp/wsbuild-clang && cd /tmp/wsbuild-clang
PKG_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/nghttp3-clang/prefix/lib/pkgconfig cmake -GNinja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
    -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=1 -DDISABLE_WERROR=1 -DENABLE_ASAN=1 -DENABLE_UBSAN=1 \
    /tmp/ws-review -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ && time ninja tshark
```

I looked into the `DECOMPRESSION_ERROR` messages. I have not found what is going on yet. 

My first idea was that decoding of the headers is blocked by QPACK lagging behind, and effectively causing a head-of-line blocking. When such condition emerges, the required QPACK insert count will be higher than the available insert count.

This isn't the case. At the time of the error, the available insert count == 2, and the required insert count == 1.

I will continue looking into this tomorrow.

+# Design notes on the HTTP3 dissector for wireshark
+
+
+## Supported features
+
+The HTTP3 dissector is a work in progress.
+
+At the moment, the following aspects of HTTP3 are supported:
+
+- Stream types
+- Frame types
+- HTTP header fields
+- QPACK insert count
+
+The future plans include adding support to:
+
+- Dissecting the SETTNIGS frames
+- Dissecting the QPACK encoder and decoder streams
+
+
+## Dissecting HTTP3 header fields
+
+HTTP3 headers are compressed with [QPACK](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-ietf-quic-qpack/).
+Because of that, the dissector needs a way to interpret the QPACK encoding
+streams, and to maintain the dynamic compression tables.
+
+Currently, the dissector relies on the QPACK compression implementation from
+`nghttp3`, which is a popular open source implementation of HTTP3.
+
+## Managing the dissector state
+
+
+### Connection-level state
+
+`nghttp3`'s QPACK implementation requires a separate dissector instance per
+QPACK encoder stream.
+
+The dissector uses `http3_session_info`, which is associated with conversation
+info pointer.
+
+NOTE: this implementation assumes that different QUIC connections will have
+different 5-tuples. Different DCIDs that share the same 5-tuple are not
+supported.
+
+### Stream-level state
+
+`nghttp3`'s QPACK implementation requires a keeping a separate context per every request stream.
+
+The dissector keeps this state in `http3_stream_info`, which is associated with
+every stream (via `quic_stream_get_proto_data`).
+
+
+### PDU-level state
+
+Finally, the header fields must be stored for reapeting access once decoding
+finishes.
+
+The dissector keeps the decoded headers in a `http3_headers_data_t`, which
+keeps the count of decoded header fields, the combined length of the fields
+after the decoding, and an array of the header fields.
+
+Similarly to the HTTP2 dissector, once the fields are decoded, they are stored in a flat buffer:
+
+```
+name_length (uint32)
+name (string)
+value_length (uint32)
+value
+```
+
+This allows using the standard Wireshark methods for parsing fields when
+constructing the decoded header field.
+
+NOTE: at the moment, header fields are not de-duped across multiple HEADERS
+frames. This limitation will be addressed later.
+
+
+```
++-----------------+
+|Packet Info      |
++-----------------+
+         |                       +-------------------+
+         |                       |http3_session_info |
+         |                       |------------------ |
+         +---conversation------->|QPACK decoders     |
+         |                       |                   |
+         |                       +-------------------+
+         |
+         |                       +--------------------+
+         |                       |http3_stream_info   |
+         |                       |-----------------   |
+         +---stream_proto_data-->|Stream context for  |
+         |                       |the QPACK decoder.  |
+         |                       |                    |
+         |                       +--------------------+
+         |                       +-------------------+
+         |                       |http3_header_data  |
+         |                       |-----------------  |
+         +---proto_data--------->|Decompressed header|
+                                 |fields.            |
+                                 +-------------------+
+```
+
+Open questions:
+1. Large files can have a lot of sessions/conversations, can use a lot of
+   memory. Maybe worth adding a setting to disable the QPACK decoding.
+2. Support for PCAPs that contain multiple DCIDs with same 5-tuples.
+   [Peter Wu]: this should be possible by somehow accessing the QUIC
+               conversation that the HTTP/3 session is layered upon.
+3. De-duplicate repeating header fields.
+
+
+## Using nghttp3 to decode HEADERS frames
+
+### Updating QPACK states
+
+When dissecting QPACK encoder stream, the dissector passes the payload to the
+corresponding `nghttp3_qpack_decoder` instance.
+
+On a successful update, the dissector appends the current insert count to the
+protocol tree.
+
+On failure, the dissector emits expert info advise.
+
+### Decompressing HTTP3 headers
+
+When dissecting HEADERS frames, the dissector attempts to decode data using the
+corresponding `nghttp3_qpack_decoder` and `nghttp3_qpack_stram_context`
+instances.
+
+The `nghttp3_qpack_decoder` informs the dissector on the decoding status via a flag word.
+
+If the decoder successfully inflates a header field, as indicated by `EMIT`
+flag bit, the output from the decoder is converted into `http3_header_field`
+and added to `http3_header_data` that corresponds to the PDU.
+
+Occasionally, the dissector can become blocked on the QPACK stream. This
+happens when decoding of the headers field depends on a QPACK update that has
+not been seen yet. The dissector indicates such condition via the
+`http3.header.qpack.blocked` flag.
+
+In addition, sometimes the decoder does can not proceed with decoding. This can
+happen, for example, when the start of the QPACK encoder stream is not present
+in the capture file.  The dissector indicates such condition via the
+`http3.header.qpack.fatal` flag.
+
+
+In addition to the flags, the dissector emits appropriate expert info when the
+decoding is not possible.
+
+### Fields to expose
+
+- `http3.stream_type`
+- `http3.frame_type`
+- `http3.frame_length`
+- `http3.frame_payload`
+- `http3.push_id`
+- `http3.header` - flag.
+- `http3.header.count` - number of fields in the HEADERS frame.
+- `http3.header.length` - the length of the fields after inflation.
+- `http3.header.name` - header field's name, after inflation.
+- `http3.header.name.length` - length of the header fields's name, after inflation.
+- `http3.header.value` - header field's value, after inflation.
+- `http3.header.value.length` - length of the header fields's value, after inflation.
+- `http3.header.qpack.blocked` - inflation of header fields is blocked on QPACK.
+- `http3.header.qpack.fatal` - inflation of header fields is not possible.
+- `http3.qpack.enc` - flag.
+- `http3.qpack.enc.icnt` - the instruction count after processing the QPACK encoder payload.
+
+
+## Open questions:
+1. Where to store the header data that could not be decoded due to QPACK
+   insertion count?  Initially, just indicate that it is blocked and append the
+   hex data to the headers dissection tree.
+2. What happens if after the decoding has finished successfully, the HEADERS
+   frame contains more data? This is more relevant to the protocol developers
+   and not to the users. Probably should have an Expert info.

+        [ -f nghttp3-$NGHTTP3_VERSION.zip ] || curl -L -o nghttp3-$NGHTTP3_VERSION.zip https://github.com/ngtcp2/nghttp3/archive/$NGHTTP3_VERSION.zip || exit 1
+        $no_build && echo "Skipping installation" && return

+uninstall_nghttp3() {
+    if [ ! -z "$installed_nghttp3_version" ] ; then
+        echo "Uninstalling nghttp3:"
+        cd nghttp3-$installed_nghttp3_version
+        # nghttp3 does not provide `make uninstall`
+        # but it leaves `install_manifest.txt` file
+        # with the paths of installed files.
+        cd build_dir
+        [ -f install_manifest.txt ] || exit 1
+        cat install_manifest.txt | while read -r FNAME ; do
+            rm "$FNAME"
+        done
+        # One caveat is that the directories
+        # $install_location/share/doc/nghttp3 and
+        # $install_location/include/nghttp3

+        done
+        cd ../..
+        rm nghttp3-$installed_nghttp3_version-done
+
+        if [ "$#" -eq 1 -a "$1" = "-r" ] ; then
+            #
+            # Get rid of the previously downloaded and unpacked version.
+            #
+            rm -rf nghttp3-$installed_nghttp3_version
+            rm -rf nghttp3-$installed_nghttp3_version.zip
+        fi
+
+        installed_nghttp3_version=""
+    fi
+}

commits_data.message:
HTTP3: Using nghttp3 to decode HTTP3 headers

Addressed comments:

https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/409#note_424651198

nghttp3: update to latest master for further fixes, build libs only

Build library only without sample applications. Use latest master which
has additional fixes:

    $ git log --abbrev=12 --oneline upstream/draft-28..upstream/master ':lib/nghttp3_qpack*'
    73eed4768e7b s/Without Name Reference/With Literal Name/
    c07e19fef3d2 Remove redundant stream object lookup
    d9a6eaefed49 Fix Insert Without Name Reference encoding
    5a3d225c477d Reduce qpack map size
    c83b1fe8e75e Pre-compute hash of known headers which is not in stable table
    6c926bb01b4c Only store known header fields to dynamic table for now

http3: fix some -Wc++-compat warnings

Addresses GCC 10.2.0 warnings:

    epan/dissectors/packet-http3.c: In function ‘decode_http3_header_data’:
    epan/dissectors/packet-http3.c:298:38: warning: request for implicit conversion from ‘void *’ to ‘http3_header_data *’ {aka ‘struct _http3_header_data *’} not permitted in C++ [-Wc++-compat]
      298 |     http3_header_data *header_data = p_get_proto_data(wmem_file_scope(), pinfo, proto_http3, 0);
          |                                      ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
    epan/dissectors/packet-http3.c:311:25: warning: request for implicit conversion from ‘void *’ to ‘guint8 *’ {aka ‘unsigned char *’} not permitted in C++ [-Wc++-compat]
      311 |         guint8 *pdata = tvb_memdup(wmem_file_scope(), tvb, offset, length);
          |                         ^~~~~~~~~~
    epan/dissectors/packet-http3.c: In function ‘dissect_http3_headers’:
    epan/dissectors/packet-http3.c:400:43: warning: request for implicit conversion from ‘void *’ to ‘http3_header_field *’ {aka ‘struct _http3_header_field *’} not permitted in C++ [-Wc++-compat]
      400 |             http3_header_field *dec_hdr = wmem_array_index(header_data->headers, i);
          |                                           ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
    epan/dissectors/packet-http3.c:417:43: warning: request for implicit conversion from ‘void *’ to ‘http3_header_field *’ {aka ‘struct _http3_header_field *’} not permitted in C++ [-Wc++-compat]
      417 |             http3_header_field *dec_hdr = wmem_array_index(header_data->headers, i);
          |                                           ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
    epan/dissectors/packet-http3.c: In function ‘dissect_http3_qpack_enc’:
    epan/dissectors/packet-http3.c:539:24: warning: request for implicit conversion from ‘void *’ to ‘const uint8_t *’ {aka ‘const unsigned char *’} not permitted in C++ [-Wc++-compat]
